covers: how to find the area of a trapezoid by averaging both parallel bases and multiplying by the perpendicular height

intro.caption: Lesson 5-3 — area of trapezoids. Two teams race to plank a trapezoid bridge span across the gorge. Only the crew with the exact area wins the build-off.

balloons.t: The bridge span is a trapezoid—narrower on top, wider on the bottom.
Blurb! Good thing I saved half the blueprint from my stomach!
Just use the bottom base, 12! Wait—or the top base, 8?
Neither alone! Average both parallel bases first, then multiply by height.

pages.caption: A trapezoid has two parallel bases of different lengths, b₁ and b₂. Averaging them gives the middle width.

balloons.t: Add b₁ and b₂, take half, then multiply by the perpendicular height!
Use the formula A = ½(b₁ + b₂) × h on the bridge ramps.
And keep that carpenter square straight! No slanted sides.
Flip and join two matching trapezoids, and boom—one giant parallelogram with base b₁ + b₂!
So one trapezoid is half of (b₁ + b₂) × h. That's why the formula works!
Bottom base is 18, height is 8. So 18 × 8 = 144 square blocks!
They ignored the 12-block top! Let's get the real plank count!
120 square blocks, 30 planks, zero gaps. Build-off champions!

win.caption: Every trapezoid is half of a parallelogram with base (b₁ + b₂) and height h, so A = ½(b₁ + b₂) × h.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Average the Bases
gates.prompt: Find the average of the two parallel bases (8 and 12), then find the trapezoid's area with height 5.
hints: Conceptual: a trapezoid's average width is halfway between its top base and bottom base.
Procedural: add b₁ + b₂, divide by 2 to get the average base, then multiply by the height.

worked.q: A trapezoid has bases 5 and 9, and height 6. What is its area?

fb.msg: 20 is 8 + 12. Divide by 2 to find the average of the two bases.
4 is 12 − 8. Add the two bases, then divide by 2.

items.label: Trapezoid area (average base 10, height 5):
items.aria: area of trapezoid deck in square blocks

fb.msg: 40 is 8 × 5, using only the top base. That misses the wider bottom!
60 is 12 × 5, using only the bottom base. That counts too much.

items.fbDefault: Multiply the average base (10) by the height (5).

gates.pass: Average base 10, area 50 square blocks! Right between 40 and 60.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Compute the Area
gates.badge: Formula Pro — A = ½(b₁ + b₂) × h
gates.prompt: Compute the areas of the ramp section and support wall using A = ½(b₁ + b₂) × h.
hints: Conceptual: add the two parallel bases first inside parentheses, then take half and multiply by the perpendicular height.
Procedural: ignore any slanted side; only the two parallel bases and the 90° height go into ½(b₁ + b₂) × h.

worked.q: Find the area of a trapezoid with bases 4 and 10 and height 5.

items.label: Ramp section (b₁ = 6, b₂ = 14, h = 7). Area =
items.aria: area of ramp section in square blocks

fb.msg: 98 is 14 × 7, using only the bottom base.

items.fbDefault: Add 6 + 14, take half, then multiply by 7.

items.label: Support wall (b₁ = 9, b₂ = 15, slant = 8, h = 6). Area =
items.aria: area of support wall in square blocks

fb.msg: 96 used the slanted side (8) instead of the perpendicular height (6).

gates.pass: 70 and 72 square blocks. The ramps lock into place!

gates.title: Gate 3 · Compare Methods
gates.badge: Method Judge — Why the Formula Works
gates.prompt: Compare Kai's single-base shortcut with Ana's two-trapezoid parallelogram proof.
hints: Conceptual: flipping and joining two identical trapezoids forms a parallelogram with base (b₁ + b₂) and height h.
Procedural: one trapezoid is always half of that combined parallelogram.

steps: Two together make a parallelogram with base 5 + 9 = 14 and area 14 × 4 = 56.
One trapezoid is half: 56 ÷ 2 = 28 square blocks.
worked.q: Two matching trapezoids (bases 6 and 8, height 7) form a parallelogram. What is ONE trapezoid's area?

items.q: Kai says a trapezoid with bases 4 and 10 and height 6 has area 4 × 6 = 24. What is wrong?

options.t: He only used the shorter base, leaving out the wider bottom

options.fb: We take half of (b₁ + b₂) × h, never multiply by 2.

options.t: He used the slanted side instead of 6
options.fb: 6 is the height, not a slanted side. His error is using only one base.

items.q: Ana joins two matching trapezoids (bases 4 and 10, height 6) into a parallelogram. How does that prove the formula?

options.t: The parallelogram has area (4 + 10) × 6 = 84, so one trapezoid is half: 42
The parallelogram has area 4 × 10 = 40, so one trapezoid is 20
options.fb: 4 × 10 multiplies the two bases together instead of adding them and multiplying by height 6.

options.t: Each trapezoid equals the full parallelogram, so the area is 84
options.fb: It takes TWO trapezoids to make the parallelogram, so one trapezoid is half.

gates.pass: Kai nods: both bases, averaged, times height. Now for the main bridge span!

gates.title: Boss Gate · Win the Build-Off
gates.prompt: The main bridge span has top base 12, bottom base 18, and perpendicular height 8. Find the area and plank count to beat The Champs.
hints: Conceptual: find the trapezoid area using both bases, then divide by how much one plank covers.
Procedural: Area = ½ × (12 + 18) × 8. Then divide that area by 4 square blocks per plank.

steps: At 5 square blocks per plank, 65 ÷ 5 = 13 planks.
worked.q: A trapezoid span has bases 8 and 12, and height 9. What is its area?

items.label: Lock 1 · Bridge span area (b₁ = 12, b₂ = 18, h = 8):
items.aria: area of main bridge span in square blocks

fb.msg: 96 is 12 × 8, using only the top base.
144 is 18 × 8 — that's The Champs' mistake, using only the bottom base!

items.label: Lock 2 · Planks needed (4 sq blocks per plank):

fb.msg: 36 planks would cover 144 square blocks — The Champs' wrong number.
480 is 120 × 4. Divide the total area by 4 to count planks.

items.fbDefault: Divide 120 square blocks by 4 square blocks per plank.

items.q: Lock 3 · Why did The Champs' 18 × 8 = 144 bridge lose the build-off?

options.t: They used only the bottom base times height instead of averaging both bases

options.fb: They did not use ½ at all — they just multiplied 18 × 8.

options.t: They measured the river width instead of the height
options.fb: 8 is the height; their error was ignoring the 12-block top base.

gates.pass: 120 square blocks, 30 planks! The bridge locks across the gorge and the trophy is ours.

journal.heading: Lesson 5-3 — what the bridge build-off taught us
rows: Area of a trapezoid = ½(b₁ + b₂) × h, where b₁ and b₂ are the two parallel bases.
Adding b₁ + b₂ and dividing by 2 gives the middle width of the trapezoid.
Flipping and joining two identical trapezoids makes a parallelogram with base (b₁ + b₂) and height h.
Using only one base × height over-counts or under-counts the area.
journal.quote: "Both bases get a vote—and I get the crumbs." — Gel

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 5-3 (Determine the Area of Trapezoids). Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. Covers averaging parallel bases, A = ½(b₁ + b₂) × h, deriving the formula from two joined trapezoids, and avoiding single-base errors.
